reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes BitConnect by promising unusually high returns, instructing viewers to deposit Bitcoin, convert it to tokens, agree to terms, and confirm a loan payment. It solicits sign-ups through a team link and offers 7% from recruited users' deposits, while citing the speaker's payout and account statements as reasons to join; the records do not show whether the advertised returns were delivered or whether viewers lost money.

citations.quote: all you have to do is deposit bitcoin onto the website convert over to tokens on the BCC Exchange on the left and your pretty much ready to do your loan
I'll be getting that capital release back after 239 days. And of course, I'll be earning interest throughout that entire period.
I have 1,783 people on my team
Basically you earn 7% of whatever that person deposits onto you.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does not present returns as a fixed certainty. He acknowledges that the market can move against an investor and describes recent interest rates as low and choppy. His calculation uses an average return, while his account of future rates is expressly hopeful. Those qualifications matter: the video can be read as personal investment commentary about changing conditions, not a promise that every viewer will earn the projected amount.

citations.quote: sometimes when the market's going down things aren't looking too good
Let's check out the average ROI on that.
there's some really low interest rates here on bit connect within the last few days it's been a little bit choppy
hopefully those interest rates start picking up a little bit more

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited capital-release statement describes what he expects from his own loan; it does not establish that he guarantees that outcome to viewers. The opening also concedes that the records do not show whether the advertised returns were delivered or whether viewers lost money. The discussion of low, choppy rates is relevant context when assessing whether his figures are unconditional promises.

citations.quote: I'll be getting that capital release back after 239 days.
there's some really low interest rates here on bit connect within the last few days it's been a little bit choppy

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Acknowledging variable rates does not undo the solicitation. The speaker recommends a minimum loan, projects substantial profit and tells viewers to join through his link. Those are promotional claims about a lending-return opportunity, even if the precise return is not guaranteed.

citations.quote: I always recommend doing a $1,000 loan or more as much as you can afford.
that's a ROI of 248 percent total profit of $2,510
click the link down below in the description. Sign up on BIC Connect if you're not already.

opening.argument: Judge, much of the video follows the speaker's own account activity. He explains how Bitcoin is converted to tokens, walks through what appears in the lending wallet on capital release, confirms his own loan, and then shows his transaction history and wallet. That sequence has a concrete instructional purpose: explaining how the interface and account balances work. The cited actions demonstrate his use of the system; they do not independently establish that another viewer will receive the same result.

citations.quote: all you have to do is deposit bitcoin onto the website convert over to tokens on the BCC Exchange on the left and your pretty much ready to do your loan
When you get your capital release it shows up in your lending wallet and u.s Dollar form
so let's agree to the terms pay from bitconnect wallet hit confirm
let's go over here to my transaction history i want to show you guys my bitcoin wallet

rebuttal.rebuttal: The deposit and conversion instructions cited in the opening are also the steps needed to understand the operation he demonstrates. The team count describes his account; by itself, it proves neither a viewer's future earnings nor that the walkthrough is solely a recruitment pitch. His first-person account and transaction-history discussion are context the opening gives too little weight.

citations.quote: all you have to do is deposit bitcoin onto the website convert over to tokens on the BCC Exchange on the left
let's go over here to my transaction history i want to show you guys my bitcoin wallet

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A walkthrough can still be promotion. Here the operational steps lead into an unusually high projected return, an explicit recommendation to lend as much as the viewer can afford, and an invitation to sign up through the speaker's team link. Showing his own account does not verify that viewers will obtain the projected return.

citations.quote: that's a ROI of 248 percent total profit of $2,510
I always recommend doing a $1,000 loan or more as much as you can afford.
if you guys want to join my team, click the link down below in the description. Sign up on BIC Connect

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker describes a referral program in concrete terms and discloses its incentive: he says a participant earns 7% of another person's deposit. The description also contains a separate purchase-discount offer. Neither statement alone proves that a viewer was deceived, that anyone was denied a withdrawal, or that the referral percentage was paid. The speaker says he has recently withdrawn Bitcoin, though that remains his own account rather than independent verification. On this record, the referral component can be understood as an openly described promotion, without treating the external service as certified safe.

citations.quote: Basically you earn 7% of whatever that person deposits onto you.
Use code "KZxUME" and get 3% off every purchase on Genesis Mining!
within the last few hours last few days i've been successfully withdrawing bitcoin here here's all my transactions

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies deposits, a team link, and a stated referral rate, but those facts do not establish an unseen payment failure or prove that the rate was misrepresented. The speaker openly identifies the deposit-based incentive. His withdrawal claim should be treated as his claim, not proof of the service's safety, but it is part of the context in which he presents the offer.

citations.quote: Basically you earn 7% of whatever that person deposits onto you.
within the last few hours last few days i've been successfully withdrawing bitcoin here here's all my transactions

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Proof of an actual loss or failed withdrawal is not needed to identify what this video promotes. The speaker directs viewers to deposit Bitcoin for lending, recommends loans of $1,000 or more, projects a 248% return, and asks them to join his team for deposit-based referral earnings. A separate purchase discount does not change the central lending and recruitment pitch.
